summary: Today the reply journey happens almost entirely outside the app. The extension already captures every notice, its PDF and the full case folder, including structured portal JSON with section, FY, reply due date, PH option, officer and the demand details (dmddtls). None of that structure is used downstream. Per the repo, the only per-notice drawer selects gst_notices.hearing_date, a column the repo's own commit 50e12fc says does not exist, so it renders 'Notice not found'. The same select silently empties the alert digests. The Sweep queries a gst_case_folder_items.notice_id column that no migration defines, and its due-date extractor reads the wrong JSON paths, so case notices (DRC-01A/DRC-01/ASMT-10) never get a due date: 0 of 403 in the 13-Sep-2026 review. matter_deadlines is never written. Filing is recorded by hand: reply_date was set on 0 rows while 121 REPLY items sat in the synced case folders. Every PDF sits in a public bucket with anon read/write/delete. There is no issue table, no evidence linkage, no drafting workspace, no client document requests and no precedent library. A typical ASMT-10/DRC-01A costs about 8.5 staff-hours and 12-25 elapsed days, most of it re-keying and hunting data the app already holds: as-filed GSTR-1/3B JSON, 2A/2B documents, ITC/RCM/suspended ledgers, DRC-03, the GSTR-9 'Notice reply format' and the interest/late-fee engines. The Reply Factory has five parts. (0) Fix the plumbing: private bucket with signed URLs, the hearing_date/notice_id drift, due dates, a DB-trigger event log, REPLY auto-reconcile and a deadline engine. (1) Add a notice_issues model fed by portal JSON plus claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 extraction (schema-validated, every field quote-verified, portal JSON wins on conflict). (2) Add deterministic recipes that turn the existing month-level reports into FY annexures with row provenance. (3) Draft with claude-opus-5-5 using cached statute/template packs and citations, behind hard gates: every rupee figure must trace to an annexure cell, and only authorities from a verified library may be cited. QA runs on claude-sonnet-5. (4) Partner approval, then a DOCX/PDF pack, then extension-assisted filing that stops before DSC/EVC and captures the acknowledgement automatically. Targets: ASMT-10/DRC-01A from about 520 to about 105 staff-minutes, first draft within 1 working day, DRC-01B/01C answered the same day, and 95% of filings recorded with no typing.

currentJourney.step: 1. Notice issued on the portal (View Notices & Orders, or an Additional Notices & Orders case folder)
currentJourney.who: Proper officer / GSTN -> client's registered email and mobile
currentJourney.pain: The firm is not the addressee. It learns at the next Sync All or when the client forwards the email. Short-clock forms (DRC-01B/01C 7 days, REG-17/REG-23 7 working days, RFD-08 15 days, MOV-07) can lose most of their window before anyone in the firm sees them.

currentJourney.step: 2. Run Sync All through the Chrome extension
currentJourney.where: App -> Chrome extension -> portal APIs (get/notices, litserv case/task/get, case/folder/items, document downloads)
currentJourney.pain: Manual and serial, with a human CAPTCHA per client login. A full run for about 121 clients takes hours; the review record noted 92 clients could not finish inside the old 20-minute job window. Case/task rows (DRC-01, ASMT-10, Enforcement, Appeal) are saved with due_date, status and issued_by = null (extension/content.js:2807). The structured folder JSON is stored but never parsed into fields. The 5 minutes shown is each notice's share of the run.

currentJourney.step: 3. Run the Sweep (auto-close and due-date extraction)
currentJourney.pain: Both passes select and filter gst_case_folder_items.notice_id, a column no migration or generated type defines (src/lib/noticeAutoClose.ts:44-45,164-165), so the sweep errors out. Even if fixed, extractDueDate reads sdtls.duedate, dtscn.duedate and duedate (lines 139-142), but the live-confirmed fields are duedt, sdtls.<dtscn|srscn|remnd>.duedt and replyDuedt (AdditionalNoticeFolderPage.tsx:168,176). Review record, 13-Sep-2026: 0 of 403 case rows had a due date.

currentJourney.step: 4. Triage: open the notice, read the PDF, set status, priority, owner, due date and amount
currentJourney.where: App drawer or list 'Log reply / order / submission' dialog + PDF viewer
currentJourney.pain: The drawer query selects the non-existent gst_notices.hearing_date and drops the error, so it shows 'Notice not found' (NoticeDrawer.tsx:144,200-201). FY, amount, extended due date, free-text assign_to and remarks are re-keyed by hand (NoticeWorkflowListView.tsx:541-555). Section, DIN, tax periods, the issue list and head-wise demand have no field at all. Four different status vocabularies are in use.

currentJourney.step: 5. Create a litigation matter and type the demand
currentJourney.where: App - drawer 'Create Matter' or Litigation Matters page
currentJourney.pain: Tax, interest, penalty and cess are typed by hand from DRC-01/DRC-02 (LitigationMatterDetailPage.tsx:482-490, no event logged), although dmddtls in the folder JSON already carries them. The matter gets the original rather than the extended due date, no actor, and lifecycle 'demand' whatever the form.

currentJourney.step: 6. Tell the client and request documents
currentJourney.pain: There is no request list, status or reminder ladder (roadmap item 1.6 is unbuilt). Files come back over email/WhatsApp into local folders, not onto the notice. Typically 3-10 elapsed days, often the longest wait in the journey (estimate).

currentJourney.step: 7. Hunt for data: pull and export returns, 2A/2B and ledgers; fetch e-way bills and supplier status elsewhere
currentJourney.where: App Reports (client + month), extension pulls, GST portal, e-way bill portal, taxpayer search
currentJourney.pain: Every comparison report takes one client and one month (src/lib/reportsCatalog.ts:251-300, 845-891), so an FY notice needs 12 runs of several reports, plus chasing NOT PULLED gaps. E-way bills, supplier cancellation dates, e-invoices and client documents are not in the app at all.

currentJourney.step: 8. Build the reconciliation working in Excel
currentJourney.where: Excel (copy-paste from app exports and Tally books)
currentJourney.pain: Re-keys numbers the app already computes: GSTR-1 vs 3B, 3B vs 2B/2A, RCM vs ITC, interest, Rule 42. Figures carry no provenance and formula errors creep in. The GSTR-9 'Notice reply format' (src/components/gstr9/steps/NoticeStep.tsx:166-171) sits unused in another module.

currentJourney.step: 9. Find a precedent reply and the law
currentJourney.where: Shared drive, old emails, CBIC website, case-law databases
currentJourney.pain: No template or precedent library. 121 past REPLY items with attachments across 68 cases (review record) are captured in the case folders but are unindexed and unsearchable.
Boilerplate is retyped for every notice, figures are transcribed from Excel, and issue coverage is checked by eye. Estimates: an s.73/74/74A SCN takes 2-4 h; a DRC-01B/01C explanation 20-40 min.
No review queue or version history in the app, and approvals are not recorded. One to three cycles add 1-4 elapsed days.

currentJourney.step: 12. Finalise the pack: letterhead, client signature or authorisation, PDF merge, compress or split for the portal
currentJourney.where: Word/PDF tools; courier or email for the signature
currentJourney.pain: Files are juggled by hand to fit the portal's attachment limits (verify the current limits). The client signature round-trip adds 1-2 days.

currentJourney.where: GST portal: case folder -> Notices -> Reply (ASMT-11 / DRC-06 / DRC-01A Part B / RFD-09) or Return Compliance (DRC-01B/01C)
currentJourney.pain: A fresh login with CAPTCHA. The extension's 'Portal' icon lands only on the generic Notices & Orders list (extension/content.js:514-523). Reply text is pasted and files attached one at a time. The OTP has to be coordinated with the client's authorised signatory.

currentJourney.step: 14. Record the filing in the app
currentJourney.pain: Reply Ref No., Reply Date and Submission ARN are typed by hand (NoticeWorkflowListView.tsx:1124-1147). In practice this is skipped: reply_date was set on 0 rows while 121 REPLY items existed (review record), so replied notices stay 'Overdue'. Saving the dialog also wipes close_reason (lines 522, 554) and writes a free-text assign_to instead of the user id.

currentJourney.step: 15. Personal hearing and written submissions (when opted or fixed)
currentJourney.where: Officer's office or video; matter page
currentJourney.pain: The PH date sits in the folder JSON (pershrng and related fields) and is never parsed; hearings are entered by hand on the matter. There is no carry-list, and post-hearing submissions repeat steps 7-13.

currentJourney.step: 16. Order received: decide on appeal, compute limitation and pre-deposit
currentJourney.pain: No code writes matter_deadlines, so there is no appeal or rectification clock and E5 limitation alerts never fire. Pre-deposit is computed by hand, with no order-vs-reply comparison to build the grounds.

recipes.inputs: gst_filed_returns GSTR1 (summary sec_sum TTL_LIAB per head; full_json B2B/B2CL/B2CS/EXP/SEZ/CDNR/CDNUR/AT/TXPD and amendment sections) and GSTR3B (3.1(a)+(b), plus 3.1(c)/(e) for context) per month with ARN and filed_date; gstr3b_adjustments (reason, table_ref); gst_running_updates (effect_month, update_in_return); gst_drc03_filings; gst_liability_ledger_entries; intimation period and amounts from the DRC-01B (portal JSON or extraction).
recipes.computation: For every month m in the intimation period and the FY to date: D(m,head) = GSTR-1 liability - 3B liability, plus the cumulative C(m,head). Attribute the difference in order: (1) timing - GSTR-1 documents of m whose tax appears in 3B of m+k, matched by doc no/date from the GSTR-1 JSON and running-update notes; the cumulative difference should revert to about 0; (2) amendments and credit notes booked in other months; (3) advances AT/TXPD; (4) mis-tagging - RCM invoices or WOPAY exports in GSTR-1 that carry no 3.1(a) tax; (5) DRC-03 paid (ARN, date, head). Residual R(head) = cumulative minus everything explained. If R > 0: tax payable plus s.50 interest on the cash portion via interestLateFee.computeInterest, from the 3B due date to the payment date. Check R against the Rule 88C threshold (verify).
recipes.annexure: A-1 Month-wise GSTR-1 vs GSTR-3B by head (IGST/CGST/SGST/Cess) with ARNs, filing dates, difference and cumulative. A-2 Reconciling items: doc no, date, GSTIN, taxable value, tax, GSTR-1 month, 3B month, reason code. A-3 DRC-03 payments: ARN, date, head-wise. A-4 Residual and interest computation. Part B: prefilled values (reason, amount, ARN).
recipes.paragraph: "The difference of Rs {A1.diff_total} between the liability declared in GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B for {period} arises because {n} invoices carrying tax of Rs {A2.timing_total}, reported in GSTR-1 for {month}, were offered to tax in GSTR-3B for {next_month} (Annexure A-2, rows {rows}). Taken over {range}, the tax paid through GSTR-3B is not less than the liability in GSTR-1 (Annexure A-1, cumulative column). [If residual:] The balance of Rs {A4.residual} has been paid vide DRC-03 ARN {arn} dated {date} with interest of Rs {A4.interest}. There is therefore no short payment, and we request that the intimation be dropped."

recipes.issue: DRC-01C: ITC in GSTR-3B vs GSTR-2B (Rule 88D)
recipes.inputs: gst_filed_returns GSTR3B Table 4A(1)-(5), 4B(1)/(2), 4D(1) per month; twob_import_docs per period (MATCHED / MISMATCHED / INELIGIBLE / ITC_OF_OTHERS, itc_available, invoice_type incl. ISD/IMPG/CDN, gstr1_filing_date); books_register; bills_not_in_2b (reversal_month, reclaim_month, reclaimed_via_doc_id); bills_not_in_books (bill_in_2b_month, book_entry_month); gst_credit_reversal_reclaim_entries (ECRRS); itc_summaries; gst_credit_ledger_transactions (balance trail); gst_drc03_filings.
recipes.computation: Per month and head: E = ITC availed in the 3B rows the portal compares (verify) - ITC available in 2B. Attribute: (1) reclaims of earlier reversals - 4D(1)/4A(5) reclaim tied to bills_not_in_2b.reclaim_month and the ECRRS reclaim entries; (2) earlier-period 2B ITC availed now - bills_not_in_books where the 2B month precedes the claim month; (3) rows outside the comparison basis (imports, ISD, RCM); (4) 2B credit-note netting and amendments; (5) genuine excess - NOT_IN_2B items claimed and not reversed. For (5), s.50(3) interest arises only if utilised: test the daily ECL balance against the excess (Rule 88B(3); verify).
recipes.annexure: B-1 Month-wise 3B ITC vs 2B ITC by head. B-2 Reclaims: ECRRS reference, reversal month, reclaim month, amount, invoice list. B-3 Earlier-2B invoices availed this period: supplier GSTIN, invoice no/date, 2B month, ITC. B-4 Excess (if any): action taken (DRC-03 / 4B(2) reversal), ECL balance trail, interest.
recipes.paragraph: "The ITC of Rs {B1.excess} availed over GSTR-2B for {month} comprises (i) Rs {B2.total}, being re-claim of ITC reversed in Table 4B(2) of GSTR-3B for {reversal_months} on invoices that have since appeared in GSTR-2B for {months}, as shown in the Electronic Credit Reversal and Re-claimed Statement (Annexure B-2); and (ii) Rs {B3.total} on invoices that appeared in GSTR-2B for {earlier_months} and were availed in this period, within the time limit of s.16(4) (Annexure B-3). [If residual:] ITC of Rs {B4.amount} has been reversed vide {DRC-03 ARN / Table 4B(2) of {month}}; the balance in the electronic credit ledger never fell below this amount, so no interest is payable (Annexure B-4). No ITC has been availed beyond the entitlement under s.16(2)(aa) read with Rule 36(4)."

recipes.issue: ASMT-10: GSTR-1 vs GSTR-3B for the FY
recipes.inputs: As DRC-01B for all 12 months; GSTR-1 of the next FY (Apr-Nov) for current-FY documents (buildGstr1PyInCyReport); GSTR-9 / 9C (annual_return_docs tables 4/5/9/10/11/14; gstr9_table14_differential_tax); books (duties_taxes_output_monthly, books_turnover_lines); the officer's figures per head from the notice.
recipes.computation: First reproduce the officer's arithmetic (which GSTR-1 figure and which 3B rows) so the reply speaks to the same numbers. Then the month table and FY totals. Add next-FY amendments and additions for current-FY supplies, and tax paid in the next FY's 3B or via GSTR-9 Table 14. Subtract DRC-03 payments. Residual, with interest on the cash portion.
recipes.annexure: C-1 Month-wise GSTR-1 vs 3B (as A-1). C-2 Next-FY amendments and additions for current-FY documents. C-3 'Notice reply format' outward rows 1-11 from the GSTR-9 workspace (NoticeStep, PDF export exists). C-4 Payments (next-FY 3B, Table 14, DRC-03). C-5 Residual and interest.
recipes.paragraph: "The notice compares GSTR-1 (Rs {X}) with GSTR-3B (Rs {Y}) for FY {fy}. The difference is fully explained by (a) supplies of FY {fy} declared and paid in GSTR-3B for {next_fy_months} (Rs {A}; Annexures C-2/C-4, also disclosed in Tables 10/11/14 of GSTR-9), and (b) {other reasons}. The outward-liability reconciliation in Annexure C-3 shows net tax payable of Rs {C3.r11}, which [has been paid vide ... / is nil]."

recipes.issue: ASMT-10 / DRC-01: GSTR-2A/2B vs GSTR-3B ITC for the FY
recipes.inputs: GSTR-3B Table 4A/4B/4D for 12 months (gst_filed_returns); gstr2a_import_docs (periods to Dec-2021) or twob_import_docs (2B), incl. gstr1_filing_date; books_register; bills_not_in_2b / bills_not_in_books; itc_summaries; annual_return_docs (8A-8D; inward 'notice format' rows 1-9); the officer's basis from the notice (2A or 2B; which table).
recipes.computation: Supplier-wise: ITC per books vs 2A/2B vs 3B claimed. FY-level: 3B net ITC (4A - 4B + reclaims) vs 2A/2B, including 2A of later periods up to the s.16(4) cut-off. Categorise: (i) supplier filed late - the invoice appears in a later 2A/2B; (ii) supplier never filed - for periods up to 31-12-2021 use the Circular 183/15/2022 and 193/05/2023 procedure (CA certificate above the threshold, supplier certificate below; verify thresholds); from 01-01-2022 s.16(2)(aa) requires 2B; (iii) wrong GSTIN / POS / ITC_OF_OTHERS; (iv) IMPG, ISD, RCM not populated in 2A; (v) ITC already reversed or never availed.
recipes.annexure: D-1 FY reconciliation (3B vs 2A/2B vs books) by head. D-2 Supplier-wise differences with category and evidence pointer. D-3 Invoices appearing in 2A/2B of later periods (with month). D-4 Certificates required or enclosed (supplier/CA) for periods up to Dec-2021. D-5 Items reversed or paid.
recipes.paragraph: "For FY {fy}, ITC availed in GSTR-3B (net Rs {X}) exceeds the ITC auto-populated in GSTR-2A/2B (Rs {Y}) by Rs {Z}. Of this, Rs {A} relates to invoices whose suppliers furnished GSTR-1 late and which appear in GSTR-2A for {months} (Annexure D-3); Rs {B} relates to imports, ISD and reverse-charge ITC that do not populate GSTR-2A (Annexure D-1); for the balance of Rs {C}, the supplier-wise details and certificates contemplated by Circular 183/15/2022-GST, made applicable to 01-04-2019 to 31-12-2021 by Circular 193/05/2023-GST [verify], are enclosed (Annexure D-4)."

recipes.inputs: rcm_data (month, particulars, supply_type, rate-wise tax), rcm_masters (notified categories), books_purchase_lines / expense_head_mappings (GTA, legal, security, director fees, rent from unregistered persons, import of services), twob_import_docs with reverse_charge = Y, gst_rcm_liability_itc_entries (portal RCM liability/ITC statement), GSTR-3B 3.1(d), 4A(2), 4A(3); gst_cash_ledger_entries.
recipes.computation: (i) RCM liability determined from the books by notified category x rate, minus 3.1(d) declared, per month. (ii) ITC in 4A(2)+4A(3) must not exceed cumulative RCM paid; the statement's closing balance must never go negative. (iii) Supplier-declared RCM invoices in 2B vs 3.1(d). (iv) Short-paid RCM: tax plus s.50 interest; ITC is available in the same period unless blocked under s.17(5), so present the revenue-neutrality facts (the legal weight of that argument: verify from the library).
recipes.annexure: E-1 RCM register vs 3.1(d), month-wise. E-2 Category-wise RCM (GTA / legal / rent / import of services) with ledger references. E-3 Portal RCM liability/ITC statement with running balance. E-4 Short payment, DRC-03 and interest.
recipes.paragraph: "RCM liability on {categories} for FY {fy} of Rs {X} was discharged in cash in Table 3.1(d) of GSTR-3B (Annexures E-1, E-3). ITC of Rs {Y} was taken in Table 4A(3) only after payment; the RCM Liability/ITC Statement shows a non-negative closing balance in every month. The difference pointed out arises because {e.g. the notice treats freight paid to GTAs who charged tax at 12% under forward charge as RCM supplies (Annexure E-2)}."

recipes.inputs: E-way bill data, which is NOT in the app: import the e-way bill portal's 'generated by me / by others' reports, or pull them through a GSP, into a new ewb_documents table. GSTR-1 invoice-level JSON (gst_filed_returns full_json / gstr1_data.raw_json); delivery challans from the books, if available.
recipes.computation: Match e-way bills to GSTR-1 documents on doc no (normalised), date (+/- 1 month) and recipient GSTIN. Classify the unmatched: cancelled within 24 h; non-supply movements (job work, same-GSTIN transfers, SKD/line sales, exhibitions, returns - from supply type and sub-type); rejected by the recipient; invoice reported in another month; value basis (e-way bill value includes tax and charges, GSTR-1 shows taxable value); several e-way bills for one invoice; e-way bills generated by the transporter.
recipes.annexure: F-1 Summary of e-way bill value vs GSTR-1 value, by month. F-2 Matched list. F-3 Unmatched e-way bills with reason code and supporting document. F-4 Residual and tax.
recipes.paragraph: "The aggregate value of e-way bills (Rs {X}) differs from the outward supplies in GSTR-1 (Rs {Y}) because (a) e-way bills of Rs {A} were cancelled within 24 hours; (b) Rs {B} relates to movement of goods for job work under delivery challans, which are not supplies; (c) Rs {C} is the difference between e-way bill value, which includes GST, and taxable value reported in GSTR-1 (Annexure F-3)."

recipes.inputs: filing_status / gst_filed_returns.filed_date per return and period; statutory due dates and extensions (needs a due-date-extension table; verify notifications) or clients.target_date_group1/2; GSTR-3B full_json (tax payable, paid in cash / ITC per head, interest and late fee paid); gst_cash_ledger_entries (debit dates); gst_credit_ledger_transactions (ECL balance trail); client_annual_turnover (late-fee tier); gst_drc03_filings (interest paid); gst_running_updates.interest.
recipes.computation: s.50(1): cash-portion tax x 18% x days late / 365 (proviso to s.50(1) and Rule 88B(1); firm positions in docs/INTEREST_LATE_FEE_POSITIONS.md). s.50(3): interest on wrongly availed ITC only for days it was utilised - daily ECL balance vs the wrongly availed amount (Rule 88B(3); verify). Late fee: per return, per day, per head, with tier and nil caps (interestLateFee.computeLateFee). Then reconcile with the department's figure, which is often on gross tax, and deduct interest and late fee already paid.
recipes.annexure: G-1 Return-wise: due date, filed date, days late, cash portion by head, interest at 18%, paid, balance. G-2 Late fee per return with tier and cap. G-3 ECL balance trail for s.50(3). G-4 Reconciliation with the notice's computation.
recipes.paragraph: "Interest under s.50(1) is leviable only on the portion of tax paid by debiting the electronic cash ledger (proviso to s.50(1) read with Rule 88B(1)) [verify]; the notice computes interest on the gross liability of Rs {X}. Correctly computed, interest is Rs {Y} (Annexure G-1), of which Rs {Z} was paid with GSTR-3B / DRC-03 ARN {arn}. The ITC of Rs {W} treated as wrongly availed was never utilised - the credit-ledger balance never fell below that amount (Annexure G-3) - so no interest arises under s.50(3)."

recipes.inputs: books_purchase_lines (expense_head, ledger_head, taxes) and expense_head_mappings; pl_input_lines; duties_taxes_input_monthly; twob_import_docs (portal INELIGIBLE flag, supplier, taxable value, ITC); GSTR-3B 4B(1) and 4D; builder module for construction cases; the list of items the notice treats as blocked.
recipes.computation: Map expense heads to s.17(5) clauses: motor vehicles/vessels/aircraft (a, aa, ab); food, catering, beauty, health, insurance, club and fitness membership, employee travel benefits (b); works contract or construction of immovable property on own account (c, d); composition supplies (e); non-residents (f); CSR (fa; verify effective date); personal consumption (g); goods lost, stolen, written off, gifted or given as free samples (h); tax paid under s.74/129/130 (i). Compute ITC claimed per clause vs reversed in 4B(1) or not availed (4D). Test the exceptions: vehicles for transporting goods, more than 13 seats, further supply of the same category, services obligatory for employers under law.
recipes.annexure: H-1 Expense-head ITC with s.17(5) clause and treatment. H-2 Items claimed under an exception, with justification and evidence. H-3 Items reversed (3B month, row). H-4 Residual payable with interest.
recipes.paragraph: "ITC of Rs {X} on {head} was not availed, or was reversed in Table 4B(1) of GSTR-3B for {months} (Annexure H-3). ITC of Rs {Y} on {motor vehicles used for transportation of goods} falls outside s.17(5)(a) by virtue of {clause}; registration certificates and usage records are enclosed (Annexure H-2)."

recipes.issue: ITC from cancelled or non-existent suppliers
recipes.inputs: twob_import_docs / gstr2a_import_docs (supplier GSTIN, invoice, gstr1_filing_date, irn); books_register; supplier registration status with effective cancellation date and order date, which is NOT in the app (new supplier_registration_status table filled through a GSP taxpayer-search API; check the permitted method); e-way bills (not in app); bank proof and GRNs from client uploads.
recipes.computation: For each cancelled supplier, bucket invoices by date against (a) the effective date of cancellation and (b) the date of the cancellation order. (i) Before the effective date: registration was valid at the time of supply. (ii) Between a retrospective effective date and the order date: contestable - show every s.16(2) condition met (tax invoice, receipt of goods via e-way bill/GRN, invoice in 2A/2B, payment including tax through banking channels, plus Rule 37 180-day payment). (iii) After the order date: not admissible - reverse with interest. Amounts by head.
recipes.annexure: I-1 Supplier list: GSTIN, name, effective date, order date, invoice count, value and ITC per bucket. I-2 Invoice-level evidence matrix: in 2A/2B? (month), e-way bill no., GRN, payment UTR and date. I-3 Reversals made and interest.
recipes.paragraph: "The registration of {supplier} was cancelled on {order_date} with retrospective effect from {effective_date}. All {n} invoices, carrying ITC of Rs {X}, were issued while the supplier's registration was active on the portal; they are reflected in our GSTR-2A/2B for {months}; the goods were received under e-way bills {..}; and the consideration including tax was paid through banking channels (Annexure I-2). Every condition of s.16(2) is satisfied. [Authority from the firm's verified library only; the legal position on retrospective cancellation must be checked: verify.]"

recipes.inputs: twob_import_docs / gstr2a_import_docs (invoice date, 2B/2A period, gstr1_filing_date); books_register.period_month and bills_not_in_2b.reclaim_month (the month ITC was actually availed); gst_filed_returns GSTR3B.filed_date for that month; GSTR-9 filing date for the FY (if pulled); cutoff.ts; s.16(5)/(6) flags (FY 2017-18 to 2020-21; revoked registrations); the invoice list from the notice.
recipes.computation: For each invoice: FY of the invoice date; deadline = the earlier of 30 November after the FY and the date the GSTR-9 for that FY was furnished (s.16(4) as amended by Finance Act 2022; verify - the app's cutoff.ts uses 30 November only); availment date = filing date of the 3B in which the ITC was claimed. Time-barred if availment date > deadline, unless s.16(5) (returns filed up to 30-11-2021 for FY 2017-18 to 2020-21) or s.16(6) applies. Show the supplier's GSTR-1 filing date alongside, because officers often apply that date instead.
recipes.annexure: J-1 Invoice-wise: supplier GSTIN, invoice no/date, FY, 2A/2B period, supplier GSTR-1 filing date, 3B period claimed, 3B filing date, deadline, s.16(5)/(6) flag, status. J-2 Summary by status and head. J-3 Reversal or payment for genuinely late items.
recipes.paragraph: "ITC on the {n} invoices in Annexure J-1 was availed in GSTR-3B for {month}, filed on {date}, before the time limit of {deadline} under s.16(4). The notice appears to apply the date on which the supplier furnished GSTR-1, which is not the test under s.16(4). [For FY 2017-18 to 2020-21:] s.16(5), inserted by the Finance (No. 2) Act, 2024 with retrospective effect from 01-07-2017, allows ITC availed in any return filed up to 30-11-2021 [and Circular 237/31/2024-GST deals with pending demands: verify]."

recipes.issue: Rule 42/43 reversal on exempt or non-business supplies
recipes.inputs: itc_reversal_lines (rule, FY); buildRule42ShortReversalReport (src/utils/interestScrutinyReports.ts:304); GSTR-3B 3.1(c)/(e) and 4B(1); books turnover (exempt / taxable); itc_summaries (common credit).
recipes.computation: Rule 42: compute D1 and D2 monthly, then the annual true-up (verify the true-up deadline). Compare with 4B(1) reversals by month. The difference is reversed with interest, or explained (e.g. exempt turnover in the notice includes no-supply items such as interest or securities valued per the Rule 45 explanation; verify).
recipes.annexure: K-1 Monthly Rule 42 computation (T, T1-T4, C1, C2, D1, D2). K-2 Annual true-up. K-3 Reversals in 3B by month. K-4 Residual and interest.
recipes.paragraph: "Common credit was reversed each month under Rule 42 and trued up for the year in GSTR-3B for {month} (Annexures K-1 to K-3). The notice's figure treats {item} as exempt turnover, whereas {explanation}. No further reversal is required."

aiPipeline.what: Private storage with signed URLs (R-01); secrets out of git (R-02); schema drift fixed (R-03, R-04); a server-validated staff session for edge functions (R-15); credential columns excluded (R-16); client consent clause in engagement letters; ai_audit_log table.
aiPipeline.guardrails: A feature flag per client (clients.ai_consent_at / ai_opt_out); every AI endpoint refuses to run when consent or a session is missing.

aiPipeline.what: Enqueue ai_jobs(kind='extract') when a gst_notices row is first seen, when a NOTCE/INTIM/ORDRS/NOTAC folder item arrives, or when a PDF is uploaded manually. Skip LUT and DRC-03 acknowledgement rows. De-duplicate on the PDF's sha256.
aiPipeline.where: Postgres trigger on gst_notices / gst_case_folder_items -> ai_jobs table; worker = supabase/functions/notice-ai-worker on pg_cron, or the agent runner (agent/src) for long jobs
aiPipeline.guardrails: Idempotent on (notice_id, doc sha256, pipeline_version); retries with backoff; a per-day spend cap.

aiPipeline.what: Fetch the PDF from private storage with the service role. Upload it once through the Files API so extraction, drafting and QA reuse the same file_id; delete it after filing or the retention period. Classify pages (notice body, DRC-02 summary, annexure tables, relied-upon documents, Gujarati/Hindi pages). Store page_count, sha256 and per-page text in notice_documents.

aiPipeline.what: Extract to a JSON schema: form_code, sections, act(s), FY and tax periods, reference no., DIN, issue date, reply due date, PH date/time/mode/venue, officer name/designation/jurisdiction, demand by head, and issues[] (issue_code from the firm taxonomy, title, period, tax/interest/penalty per head, para no., page, source_quote), plus documents asked for and relied-upon documents.
aiPipeline.model: claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 with structured outputs (output_config.format JSON schema); escalate to claude-sonnet-5 when validators fail or the PDF exceeds 100 pages; Message Batches API (50% cost) to backfill the existing ~1,060 notices
aiPipeline.guardrails: (a) Every field carries page + verbatim source_quote, checked by substring match against the page text; the Citations API cannot be combined with structured outputs, so verification happens in code. (b) Arithmetic: issue amounts must sum to the DRC-02 / total demand per head. (c) Cross-check against portal JSON (sdtls.dtscn.sec/fy/duedt/pershrng, dmddtls): the portal value wins and conflicts are flagged. (d) Enumerated codes only, with 'OTHER' + free text allowed. (e) The due date and demand always need one-click human confirmation.

aiPipeline.what: On confirmation, or automatically when the portal JSON agrees: fill form_code, section, period, DIN, officer, due_date (with source), amount_of_demand and financial_year. Create matter_deadlines from litigation_rules (reply due, PH, order time limit under s.73(10)/74(10)/74A, appeal clock on orders). Set priority (short-clock forms = High), owner = clients.assigned_accountant, reviewer by rule, and SLA milestones (documents requested D+1, first draft at 40% of the window, partner review at 70%).

aiPipeline.what: Candidates: firm templates for (form, issue_code); past approved replies (121 REPLY items across 68 cases already synced, plus partner-final drafts going forward) with outcomes (ASMT-12 / DRC-07: dropped, confirmed, partly); and a curated legal_authorities table (statute sections, rules, circulars, judgments with verified citation, holding and date). aiPipeline.what: Structure: preliminary objections where applicable (limitation, DIN, jurisdiction, natural justice, notice beyond DRC-01A), facts, then issue-wise replies (stance, computation by annexure reference, law), then the prayer (drop proceedings, PH request). aiPipeline.where: supabase/functions/notice-ai-draft (streaming; long runs go to the worker, verify Edge Function wall-clock limits) -> reply_drafts (version, markdown, citations JSON, prompt hash, input hashes, model, usage)

Prompt caching: frozen system prompt + style guide + statute/circular pack + form template, cached with cache_control (1h TTL for morning batches; 512-token minimum on Opus 5.5), with volatile notice content after the last breakpoint. Results are written onto the draft as a checklist.

filingAssist.step: 1. Gate: 'File on portal' button on the notice page
filingAssist.automation: Full (app). Enabled only when the draft is partner-approved, the pack passes the size/format validator and no REPLY item already exists for this notice.
filingAssist.risk: Stale sync data could hide an existing reply, so step 3 re-checks live through litserv before any field is touched.

filingAssist.step: 2. Launch and log in as the client
filingAssist.automation: Assisted. The app posts __gstkPrepareReply {noticeId, clientId, caseArn, refNo, formCode, packId}; the background worker fetches the pack through short-lived signed URLs and reuses handleLogin (a human types the CAPTCHA).
filingAssist.risk: Today the portal password is copied into chrome.storage job objects (extension/background.js:304,516); fetch it at login time or have the user type it. GSTN treats automated access as unauthorised (agent/README.md 'Legal / risk'), so keep this user-initiated and attended, and never solve the CAPTCHA.

filingAssist.step: 3. Navigate to the right reply screen
filingAssist.automation: Full where selectors are known, via a versioned route map per form: case-folder notices (ASMT-10, DRC-01A, DRC-01, RFD-08) -> litserv case folder for the case ARN -> Notices/Intimations -> item with refId -> Reply; DRC-01B/01C -> Return Compliance screens; REG-03/17/23/31 -> registration reply screens (verify each path).
filingAssist.risk: Selector fragility on an Angular SPA that changes with portal releases. Assert screen identity (the on-screen reference no. must equal the notice ref) before acting; otherwise fall back to 'stop and guide' mode with copy-to-clipboard.

filingAssist.automation: Full: reply text (a summary within the field's character limit, verify; the full reply goes as the PDF), reply type, PH option, DRC-03 ARN(s) for Part B 'paid' options, DRC-01B/01C reason codes.
filingAssist.risk: Wrong field or wrong notice. Read back every filled value, highlight it, and leave the declaration and verification ticks to the human.

filingAssist.automation: Full (best effort): download the files, set input[type=file] through DataTransfer, dispatch input/change events, then confirm each filename and size appears on screen.
filingAssist.risk: The portal may ignore programmatically set files or enforce type, size or count limits (verify). Fallback: save the pack to a local folder and let the user attach it.

filingAssist.automation: Manual by design: a banner says 'Check, then sign with DSC/EVC'. The extension never clicks Submit/File/Proceed-to-sign and never touches the OTP or DSC.
filingAssist.risk: The EVC OTP goes to the authorised signatory (often the client), so the app should schedule a call slot. Users may expect auto-filing, so the UI copy must be explicit.

filingAssist.automation: Full: the content script watches the submit response or acknowledgement page (reply ARN/ref, date, ack PDF), then __gstkReplyFiled -> RPC log_reply_filed sets reply_date, reply_ref_number / submission_arn, stage 'Filed', deadline met, a reply_logged event and the matter stage; the ack PDF goes to private storage.
filingAssist.risk: Ack page formats change. Fallback: the REPLY-folder reconciler on the next sync (reply.ntcno / decdtls.dt) marks the notice filed with no typing.

filingAssist.automation: Full: create the PH deadline if one was opted for; send the client the filed copy (E13); watch for ASMT-12, DRC-07 or closure items to close the notice or open the appeal clock.
filingAssist.risk: A misclassified folder item could close a notice wrongly, so closure requires an item-type match and orders need human confirmation.

filingAssist.automation: Full: written client authorisation for portal access on file; every extension action logged with a screenshot (the agent already does screenshot audits); a per-portal-release kill switch with a canary run on a test GSTIN.
filingAssist.risk: Legal exposure (GSTN advisory, IT Act) grows sharply if this ever runs unattended or auto-submits, so both are kept out of scope permanently.

findings.issue: Every notice PDF, case-folder attachment and manual upload sits in a public bucket with anon INSERT, SELECT, UPDATE and DELETE policies, and is stored as a permanent public URL. findings.fix: Add notice_doc_requests (item, issue_id, requested_at, due, status, received_document_id), E12/E13 emails through email_outbox, and a signed client upload link. Generate the list automatically from issue codes.

findings.issue: Ownership is split between two fields. The edit dialog writes free-text assign_to only, while the work queue's Mine and Unassigned tabs use assign_to_user_id. A notice assigned in the dialog still shows as Unassigned and never appears in 'Mine'.
findings.fix: Use a staff picker that writes assign_to_user_id everywhere (derive assign_to from profiles), back-fill existing rows by name, and add reviewer_user_id to the notice.

findings.issue: Four stage vocabularies are in use: the work queue's STAGE_OPTIONS, the drawer's regex stepper, the list view's Open/Closed select, and the matter's 11 stages. The list view shows 'Set status' for a row in 'Partner review' and overwrites it with one click. Stage-based SLAs, MIS and alerts cannot be trusted.
findings.fix: Define one stage enum (Captured -> Triage -> Awaiting data -> Drafting -> Partner review -> Filed -> Hearing -> Order -> Appeal -> Closed) with a CHECK constraint. Every status select uses it, and open/closed is derived from it.

findings.issue: The activity timeline is incomplete. There is no trigger on gst_notices, and notice_events is written only by a few app paths. Bulk assign, priority and stage in the queue, and bulk status in the list, write nothing, and no code ever writes a 'captured' event. The E1 'new notice' rule therefore has no event source, and touches per notice cannot be measured.
findings.fix: Add AFTER INSERT/UPDATE triggers on gst_notices (and on folder items) that write notice_events, taking the actor from a session setting set by an RPC. Suppress events on bulk re-sync by comparing portal_hash and first_seen_at.

findings.issue: The existing edge-function pattern (verify_jwt = false, authorising on a caller-supplied actorId) must not be reused for AI. User ids are readable through the open profiles table, so an AI drafting endpoint built that way would let anyone with the anon key read any client's notice through the model and spend the firm's API budget.
findings.fix: Use a server-validated staff session (a signed token issued at authenticate_staff and verified in a shared _shared/auth.ts), with per-user rate limits and an ai_audit_log. The client role gets no access to AI endpoints.

findings.issue: Portal passwords are stored in plaintext columns (clients.gst_password and client_password, profiles.password) and copied into chrome.storage job objects. Any AI context builder that selects * from clients would send credentials to a third party, and filing assist would widen the exposure.
findings.fix: Read clients only through a clients_safe view with explicit column lists in every AI or report path. Add a redaction module (_shared/ai/redact.ts) with a deny-list test, encrypt credentials at rest, and keep passwords out of job objects by fetching them at login time.

findings.issue: Saving the edit dialog for any reason wipes close_reason, because the field is initialised blank and written as null. This erases 'auto:closure' tags and logs a spurious change.
findings.fix: Prefill closeReason from the row, and write only the fields the user changed.

findings.issue: Documents are scattered and incomplete. The drawer shows only pdf_url, case-folder attachments appear only on the folder page, and the matter's 'Add Document' stores a title with no file, even though matter_documents has storage_path, mime and size_bytes columns.
findings.fix: Build a unified documents panel (portal PDF, all folder attachments, uploads, drafts, acknowledgements) backed by notice_documents with kinds, versions, sha256 and signed URLs.

findings.issue: There is no deep-linkable notice page. The drawer mounts only on the dashboard and no /notices/:id route exists, so alert emails, the queue and teammates cannot link to a specific notice (roadmap 2.6).
findings.fix: Add NoticeDetailPage at /notices/:id implementing perNoticeSpec, and reduce the drawer to a peek with 'Open full page'.

findings.issue: The work queue fetches .limit(1000) across all notices, closed ones included, and filters out closed rows client-side, so open notices beyond the cap silently disappear. It also sorts newest-issued first while its pill says 'earliest due first'.
findings.fix: Filter to open notices server-side and ORDER BY effective due date (nulls last), using fetchAllRows or a view/RPC. Fix the label.

findings.issue: Payments are not linked. DRC-03 filings are synced with head-wise amounts, but matter payments are typed by hand (drc03_arn is never captured), and paid_total is updated read-modify-write from stale page state, so concurrent updates are lost.
findings.fix: Auto-link gst_drc03_filings to notices and matters by ARN, period and cause (suggest, then confirm), and compute paid and pre-deposit totals in a SQL view.

findings.issue: Matter numbering and status are inconsistent. Two generators (per-year max+1 and global count+1) can produce duplicate matter_no values. The list page creates status 'open' while the detail page tests status === 'Open', so a matter created from the list shows 'Reopen' instead of 'Close'.
findings.fix: Use a DB sequence or unique constraint for matter_no, a status enum with a CHECK constraint, and a single createMatter path.

findings.issue: s.16(4) ineligible ITC is a typed input in the GSTR-9 notice format, and the cut-off helper uses 30 November only. The provision as amended by Finance Act 2022 reads '... or furnishing of the relevant annual return, whichever is earlier' (verify). The inputs needed to compute it (2B gstr1_filing_date, 3B filing dates) are already in the database.
findings.fix: Build the s.16(4) recipe: deadline = min(30 November, GSTR-9 filing date), with s.16(5)/(6) flags and an invoice-level annexure. Feed the GSTR-9 row from it.

findings.issue: Manual notices (physical or emailed: summons, ADT-01, MOV-07, GSTAT, many state notices) are keyed into an 8-field dialog with type 'Notice' or 'Order' only, and the attachment goes to the public bucket. There is no PDF-to-fields extraction.
findings.fix: Make the flow upload-first: PDF -> private storage -> extraction stage -> prefilled form for confirmation.

findings.issue: Work starts late because nothing is scheduled before the deadline. The drawer warns only inside 7 days and ignores reply_date, there are no internal milestones (documents requested, first draft, partner review), and isDueIn7 also counts notices that have already been replied to.
findings.fix: Add SLA milestones per form (documents requested D+1, first draft at 40% of the window, partner review at 70%) that drive queue sorting and alerts, and exclude replied notices from due-soon.

findings.issue: Capture latency is bound to people. Notices arrive only when someone runs Sync All and types a CAPTCHA for each client, and the 'Portal' button logs in but lands on the generic Notices & Orders list rather than the notice's case folder or reply screen.
findings.evidence: extension/content.js:361 (handleLogin), 514-523; agent/README.md (CAPTCHA posture; unattended sync is Phase 4, not built)
findings.fix: Schedule an agent pull with a CAPTCHA inbox (roadmap Phase 4), and add a per-form deep-link route map to the case folder, which filing assist will reuse.

findings.issue: 'Create Matter' from the drawer uses the original rather than the extended due date, passes no actor, and hard-codes lifecycle 'demand' with title = notice_type. Lifecycle vocabularies also differ between LIFECYCLES (lowercase) and LIFECYCLE_HINTS ('Assessment', 'Scrutiny').
findings.fix: Derive lifecycle from the form code, carry the effective due date and the actor, and link the notice in the same transaction (RPC).

findings.issue: The case-folder page hides useful facts: 'Reply Type' and 'Original Due Date' are always blank, the officer column shows only the designation (todtls.dg), and the fallback dump drops arrays. These are exactly the fields the issue table and header need.
findings.fix: Parse these into typed columns at sync (notice header facts and notice_issues) instead of rendering raw JSON.
